sections.heading: 1. On the table
lines: ① Aim for about 5–7 out of 10.
② Holding your breath? Say so straight away.
③ Deep work: slow and sustained, not hard.
④ After: a 10-minute walk or your exercises.

ask for lighter pressure next time.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
Does a massage have to hurt to work? Usually, no.

'No pain, no gain' sticks around, but research suggests much of the benefit comes from helping your nervous system settle. If you're gripping the table and holding your breath, your muscles are more likely to guard than let go.

A useful guide is around 5–7 out of 10, where you can still breathe slowly. Firm work can be slow and sustained rather than forceful. Some tenderness the next day is common; bruising or feeling worse for days is a sign to dial it back.

Massage complements active rehab, so follow it with a walk or your exercises. Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio check in on pressure as they go. Book online via the link in bio.
